name: Al Kapone
notes: A crunk-chant *songwriter*, and the research says his writing is shouted-chant-first: the melodic layer is a 1–2 bar brass/organ ostinato, with **no sustained melody and no countermelody**. So the melody block is short-phrase and stab-shaped (`phraseBars` weighted to 1 and 2, `motifPitchCount` 2–4, `timbreHint` `synth_brass_stab`) and the harmony is not a progression but two events: brass/organ stabs on i and ♭VI supply the *only* harmonic movement, which is what the i / i–VI / i–♭II families with `impliedByRiff` encode. The drums carry the rest. Two described things are unusual for this axis: **marching snare figures under the chant**, authored as the highest snare `ghost.prob` in the batch spread across four 16th positions, and **32nd roll crescendos as the only transition device**, which is why the roll ramps to 106 with a low `gapProb`. The 808 is saturated with a second distorted synth-bass octave beneath it, so `bass808.distortion` is heavy and `bassline.register` opens to 19 semitones to reach the doubled octave. Arrangement is call-and-response with crowd-response gaps and a full drop-out to claps and a cappella chant — `dropOutBeats.prob` 0.85 is the highest here for that reason. ⚠ `medium`: the research rates it medium — the crunk-songwriting credits and the soundtrack role are sourced, but **the drum and tempo values are crunk-lane anchored rather than documented for him** (76–86 half-time = 152–172 straight, marked [LOW-CONF] and pinned to the lane's 78 BPM figure), so `session.bpm` and the kick placement are the inferred ones. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 43 to 41 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 42 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 2. ⚠ `anticipationProb` raised to 0.15. With `mirror_kick` against a fully locked 808 both parts take every kick, so every bass onset lands exactly on an 808 onset — `coherence.rs` calls that one line played twice rather than two parts locking. The lock is the style and is untouched; the anticipation is what makes them two parts. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 873 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [2,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
